metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (Ruby controller with CRUD endpoints) is present with an implied deployable entry point (Rails 2.3 application deployed on EC2 per README). Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Database connections (MySQL via find_by_sql), write endpoints (create action with Order.new/save), and state mutations (order creation with payment processing) indicate a stateful CRUD service.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.18 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings maps to Remediation Required tier. The divergence arises because nearly every scored question received a 1 (lowest possible), dragging the average below 1.5, while the count-based rule caps at Remediation Required for 2-11 High findings.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: Ruby 1.8.7 and Rails 2.3 are EOL — incremental modernization within the current stack is impractical. Strangler Fig enables incremental extraction of bounded contexts into modern services while the legacy app continues operating.

approaches.name: Strengthen as Modular Monolith
approaches.reason: Not viable — Ruby 1.8.7 and Rails 2.3 are EOL with no path to modern patterns within the current stack

approaches.name: Strangler Fig (Parallel Track)
approaches.reason: Best fit — incrementally extract services while keeping legacy storefront running during transition

approaches.name: Conditional / Adaptive
approaches.reason: Alternative if capacity is constrained — selective extraction of high-value domains (payments) first

approaches.name: Big-Bang Rewrite
approaches.reason: Consider only due to small codebase size — carries typical rewrite risks

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on raw EC2 instances with Mongrel cluster behind Apache mod_proxy_balancer deployed to a fixed set of EC2 hosts. No managed container orchestration or serverless.
findings.gap: No managed compute services. All operational burden (patching, scaling, capacity planning) is manual. Mongrel is unmaintained.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed compute. Replatform to a modern language/framework and deploy on ECS Fargate or Lambda.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: MySQL 5.1 runs on a separate EC2 instance (self-managed). No managed database service is used.
findings.gap: Database is fully self-managed on EC2. No automated failover, no managed backups, no automated patching. MySQL 5.1 is EOL.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for MySQL or Aurora MySQL with automated backups, Multi-AZ failover, and automated patching.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: Order-creation workflow (create order → charge payment gateway) is entirely hardcoded in the controller with no retry logic or compensation handling.
findings.gap: Multi-step business workflow hardcoded with no orchestration, no retry strategy, and no compensation on payment failure.
findings.recommendation: Implement order processing as a Step Functions state machine with error handling, retries, and compensating transactions.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. Payment gateway call blocks the HTTP request thread. All operations are synchronous.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Payment processing tightly coupled to order creation.
findings.recommendation: Introduce managed messaging (SQS/SNS/EventBridge) to decouple order creation from payment processing.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network security configuration exists. No HTTPS termination at app tier. No VPC, subnet, or security group definitions.
findings.gap: No evidence of network segmentation, private subnets, or security groups. No HTTPS termination.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in VPC with private subnets. Configure least-privilege security groups. Add HTTPS termination via ALB.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No managed API entry point. Self-managed Apache mod_proxy_balancer with no throttling, authentication, or request validation.
findings.gap: No managed entry point. No request throttling, no centralized authentication, no DDoS protection.
findings.recommendation: Add ALB or API Gateway as entry point with HTTPS termination, throttling, and WAF integration.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configured. Fixed set of EC2 hosts with static capacity provisioning.
findings.gap: All capacity statically provisioned. Cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling on compute layer (ECS service auto-scaling or EC2 ASG) with target tracking policies.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration found. MySQL 5.1 on EC2 has no documented or configured backup strategy.
findings.gap: No automated backups. No retention period, no PITR, no restore testing. Data loss risk unmitigated.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: configure EBS snapshots. Target: migrate to RDS/Aurora with automated daily backups and PITR.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No infrastructure-as-code exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any IaC tooling. 0% coverage.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. Infrastructure changes are manual, error-prone, and non-reproducible.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in Terraform or AWS CDK. Start with database and networking layers.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration found. Deployments are manual via Capistrano 2 (config not in repo).
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deploy pipeline. All deployments are manual with no quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with build, test, security scan, and deploy stages using CodePipeline or GitHub Actions.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Ruby 1.8.7 with Rails 2.3 — both long-past EOL. Compound legacy signals: language, framework, and no AWS SDK.
findings.gap: Language version (Ruby 1.8.7 EOL), framework (Rails 2.3 EOL), and no AWS SDK. Cannot run modern gems.
findings.recommendation: Replatform to a modern language/framework (Python 3.12+, Node.js 20+, Java 21, or modern Ruby 3.3/Rails 7.x).

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith. Single controller handles order CRUD and payment processing inline. No module boundaries.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries. Payment processing directly coupled to order management.
findings.recommendation: Identify bounded contexts and extract services using Strangler Fig pattern. Start with payment domain.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP. Payment gateway SOAP call blocks the request thread. No async patterns.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous. Payment gateway calls block user requests. No decoupling.
findings.recommendation: Introduce async processing for payment operations using SQS with dead-letter queues for failed payments.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: Payment gateway SOAP call is network-bound with variable latency, handled synchronously with no timeout.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Payment calls are network-bound with unpredictable latency.
findings.recommendation: Implement payment as async operation: accept order, return pending status, process payment in background.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. No /v1/ URL patterns, no version headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly to all consumers.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (/v1/orders) in the modernized application.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All service endpoints hardcoded. Payment gateway endpoint is static URL in config/payment.yml.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hardcoded in configuration. No dynamic discovery, no service registry.
findings.recommendation: Use AWS Service Discovery (Cloud Map) or SSM Parameter Store for service endpoints.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Static assets served from the Rails app on EC2 local storage. No S3, no CDN, no managed object storage.
findings.gap: Unstructured data on local filesystem. No managed object storage, no CDN.
findings.recommendation: Move static assets to Amazon S3 with CloudFront CDN for delivery.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Database queries executed directly in controller via find_by_sql with raw SQL string interpolation. No repository pattern.
findings.gap: Database queries scattered in controllers with no pattern. Raw SQL bypasses ORM benefits.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/service layer pattern with parameterized queries and centralized data access.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: MySQL 5.1 — EOL since December 2013 (over 12 years past EOL). Known unpatched security vulnerabilities.
findings.gap: Database engine over 12 years past EOL. No security patches, no version management strategy.
findings.recommendation: Urgent: upgrade MySQL through supported path (5.1 → 5.7 → 8.0) or migrate to Aurora MySQL.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest. MySQL 5.1 on EC2 has no documented encryption. No EBS encryption, no KMS keys.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest. Database data and application data are unencrypted on disk.
findings.recommendation: Enable EBS encryption on database volume. Migrate to RDS/Aurora with KMS encryption at rest.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No API authentication mechanism. Controller comment states 'No before_filter auth on some actions (legacy oversight).'
findings.gap: No API authentication — endpoints are open. Order data accessible without identity verification.
findings.recommendation: Implement authentication on all endpoints using Cognito with JWT tokens or API Gateway authorizers.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. No Cognito, no OIDC/SAML, no SSO. No visible authentication system.
findings.gap: Application has no external IdP integration. No SSO, no federation, no centralized identity.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or external IdP for centralized authentication and SSO.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext payment credentials committed to source control in config/payment.yml (merchant_id, api_password). Session secret also in source control per README.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in version-controlled files. Payment gateway password exposed in git history.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: rotate all exposed credentials. Implement AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy. EOL Ruby 1.8.7 and Mongrel with many known CVEs. No SSM, no Inspector, no hardened AMIs.
findings.gap: No patching strategy. Runtime and application server are unmaintained with known CVEs.
findings.recommendation: Use managed compute (Fargate/Lambda) or implement SSM Patch Manager with hardened AMIs and Inspector scanning.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No CI/CD pipeline exists. Known SQL injection vulnerability persists undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning — no SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning.
findings.recommendation: Include SAST (SonarQube, Semgrep), dependency scanning, and container scanning in CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing. Cannot trace requests across application and external payment gateway.
findings.recommendation: Instrument OpenTelemetry or AWS X-Ray with trace ID propagation across all service boundaries.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLO definitions. No CloudWatch alarms, no error budget tracking, no latency targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for critical user journeys. Implement CloudWatch alarms for p99 latency and error rates.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business event tracking, no dashboards.
findings.gap: No business metrics. Cannot measure orders placed, payments succeeded/failed, or conversion rates.
findings.recommendation: Implement custom CloudWatch metrics for key business events and create stakeholder dashboards.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no incident notification.
findings.gap: No alerting. System failures invisible to operators until user complaints arrive.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms for error rates and latency. Enable anomaly detection. Integrate with PagerDuty.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: README states 'Tests are a stale Test::Unit suite that no longer runs.' No working tests exist.
findings.gap: No working tests. No integration tests for order/payment workflow. No regression safety net.
findings.recommendation: Implement integration tests covering order creation and payment workflows. Run in CI pipeline.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no CODEOWNERS, no team attribution.
findings.gap: No observability ownership. Monitoring is nonexistent.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards with named team ownership and alarm escalation paths.
